newsitem.title: UK: British Gas down, rejects Ofgas proposals.
newsitem.headline: British Gas down, rejects Ofgas proposals.

text.p: Shares in British Gas Plc dropped in early trading on Thursday after the company said it rejected price controls proposed by industry regulator Ofgas for its transmission business TransCo.
The stock was down 6p at 193-1/2 by 0704 GMT.
British Gas said the Ofgas proposals would cut TransCo's annual cash flow by 400 million stg or more and were unjustified and unworkable.

Yet the rejection means the issue will be referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission, whose inquiry could take many months to complete. Philip Hollobone, analyst at Williams de Broe, said the stock had been overshadowed for some months by the threat of a referral to the Monopolies Commission.
"It has all been about whether Gas is going to be referred to the MMC and now we know they are," Hollobone said.
"Maybe the market has suddenly woken up and lost patience. It could go on for six months and at the other side there could be a Labour government."
"People have been trying to talk up the stock," Hollobone said, "but maybe they now realise it is not going back above two pounds for the next six months and it's time to get out."
David Stedman, analyst at Daiwa Europe, said the stock's drop below 200p in May this year after an extended underperformance had prompted some to buy on recovery hopes.

"A lot of people came off the sell tack after it plunged below two pounds," Steadman said, "but given the fact that they are going to the MMC the stock is unlikely to do anything dramatic for the next few months."
Last week British Gas shares dropped on reports the natural gas supplier will seek a reference to the MMC.

The company also said last week talks had ended on the sale of parts of its business in Scotland and the north of England to Scottish Hydro Plc, which some analysts attributed to persistent commercial and regulatory pressure.
